Ids are never changed by these proposals.

C. factual-corrections-elsewhere.$comment: Found while checking that nothing in the tree claims a discrete 2 MHz C64 crystal. Not mine to edit.
2.048-MHz-quartz-crystal: metal.silica.quartz-crystal is named '2.048 MHz quartz clock crystal' and its description claims 'The C64's timing reference: an AT-cut quartz plate about 7.6 x 2.5 mm brazed between metal caps, resonating at 2.048 MHz', with a fact '2.048 MHz (PAL/NTSC master clock)'. The breadbin C64 has no such crystal: Y1 is 14.31818 MHz NTSC or 17.734475 MHz PAL in an HC-49/U can, and the 74LS629/MC4044 PLL derives the dot clock from it. The 2 MHz figure is the CPU Phi 2 output of the divider, not a crystal.

Suggested fix: delete metal.silica.quartz-crystal and re-point metal.silica's child edge at mb.crystal.y1, which already carries the full crystal chain (quartz -> synthetic autoclave -> X-ray orienting -> lapping -> grinding -> electrodes -> case). metal.silica.quartz-crystal is referenced by metal.silica only.

Also correct metal.silica's own description, which says 'A 1982 Commodore 64 mainboard carried a handful of silicon dies and one 2 MHz quartz crystal'. Say 14.31818 MHz, or say 'and one quartz crystal' and let mb.crystal.y1 carry the number.
nylon-6-6-from-caprolactam: 30-passives contained four nodes claiming nylon 6,6 was made by ring-opening polymerisation of caprolactam. That is the route to nylon 6; nylon 6,6 is hexamethylenediamine plus adipic acid. I corrected mine and deleted the caprolactam branches.

Worth a grep across the other fragments: any node whose description says nylon 6,6 (or PA66) comes from caprolactam, phenol or cyclohexanone is wrong in the same way. c64.case.other-polymers.nylon in 40-chassis already has the right inputs (adipic acid, hexamethylenediamine), which suggests the rest of that fragment agrees.
metal.silica-is-not-silica-sand: metal.silica is 'High-purity silicon feedstock (9N polysilicon)'. Several fragments listed 'metal.silica' as the ingredient of glass, glass fibre, ceramic filler, silicone rubber or quartz, which silently links a glass part to a polysilicon ingot. I replaced every such input in 30-passives with metal.silica-sand or chem.glass-fiber. The same substitution is probably needed elsewhere.
duplicate-iron-ore-leaves: Roughly a dozen fragments each carry their own inline 'Iron ore' leaf under a tool-steel or spring-steel node, always with the same boilerplate paragraph ('Hematite and magnetite, the iron ore of the world trade. Everything ferrous in this file ... begins here'). That paragraph describes the file, not the part. metal.iron is the canonical node; the tool-steel route is metal.die-steel.

keyboard-branch-duplication.$note: 40-chassis carries c64.keyboard.switches.* (19 nodes) for the C64 keyboard's switches, and 30-passives carries c64.keyboard-switches.* for the same hardware from the other direction. This is the largest remaining duplication in the tree and needs one owner. I have flagged it in B above but made no cross-fragment edit.
